done_when: The agent has the facts the decision needs: use, spending categories, any hard feature requirements (foreign transaction fee, minimum payment, virtual card management, purchase protection, a credit limit the card must be able to reach), fee tolerance or budget, the tie-break order when the customer has one, Rho-Bank+ status, invitation status, credit score (or that the customer did not give it), and monthly spend where Platinum is in play. It has checked every personal card's rates, fees, features, protection, limit range and eligibility. It has then either recommended the card or cards that meet every requirement (one card when the customer gave a tie-break order), with their rate, annual fee and requirements (including any rebate condition and minimum score), or told the customer no card fits. For a customer whose goal is a sign-up bonus, the agent has checked every card's promotion window against get_current_time. It has then either reported each open sign-up bonus that fits (bonus as stated, spend threshold, period, window and annual fee) and recommended one by the customer's tie-break, or said that none fits and why. The customer has applied with apply_for_credit_card, or has declined or chosen to go elsewhere. When the customer named a card, one of two things is true. They applied for it with their full name, annual income and Rho-Bank+ status and were told the result (with any error resubmitted or a transfer offered). Or they were told it is not available to them (Diamond Elite without an invitation, Gold without Rho-Bank+).
